title: Impact of M&A Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. This is the appropriate causal method for measuring the impact of corporate announcements on stock returns. The key assumption is that in the absence of the M&A announcement, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns (market model). We calculate abnormal returns as the difference between actual returns and expected returns based on the market model, then cumulate these over the event window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s52_data.csv")

# Define event window and estimation window
estimation_start <- -60
estimation_end <- -11
event_start <- -10
event_end <- 10

# Filter data for estimation and event windows
estimation_data <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= estimation_start & event_day <= estimation_end)

event_data <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= event_start & event_day <= event_end)

# Calculate market model parameters for each stock using estimation window
market_model_params <- estimation_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    alpha = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[1],
    beta = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[2],
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Merge parameters with event data
event_data_with_params <- event_data %>%
  left_join(market_model_params, by = "stock_id")

# Calculate abnormal returns
event_data_with_params <- event_data_with_params %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret = alpha + beta * mkt_ret,
    abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret
  )

# Calculate daily average abnormal returns across all stocks
daily_aar <- event_data_with_params %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    AAR = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_aar = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    t_stat = AAR / se_aar,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns for each stock
car_by_stock <- event_data_with_params %>%
  arrange(stock_id, event_day) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(CAR = cumsum(abnormal_ret)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate average cumulative abnormal returns
daily_caar <- car_by_stock %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    CAAR = mean(CAR, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_caar = sd(CAR, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    t_stat = CAAR / se_caar,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Print key results
cat("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n\n")

cat("Average Abnormal Return on Event Day (day 0):\n")
day_0_aar <- daily_aar %>% filter(event_day == 0)
cat(sprintf("AAR = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", day_0_aar$AAR, day_0_aar$AAR * 100))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic = %.3f\n", day_0_aar$t_stat))
cat(sprintf("Significance: %s\n", ifelse(abs(day_0_aar$t_stat) > 1.96, "Significant at 5%", "Not significant")))

cat("\nCumulative Abnormal Return [-1, +1] window:\n")
car_window <- daily_caar %>% filter(event_day %in% c(-1, 0, 1))
car_3day <- sum(daily_aar %>% filter(event_day %in% c(-1, 0, 1)) %>% pull(AAR))
car_3day_se <- sqrt(sum((daily_aar %>% filter(event_day %in% c(-1, 0, 1)) %>% pull(se_aar))^2))
car_3day_t <- car_3day / car_3day_se
cat(sprintf("CAR(-1,+1) = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", car_3day, car_3day * 100))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic = %.3f\n", car_3day_t))
cat(sprintf("Significance: %s\n", ifelse(abs(car_3day_t) > 1.96, "Significant at 5%", "Not significant")))

cat("\nCumulative Abnormal Return [-10, +10] window:\n")
car_full <- tail(daily_caar$CAAR, 1)
car_full_se <- tail(daily_caar$se_caar, 1)
car_full_t <- tail(daily_caar$t_stat, 1)
cat(sprintf("CAR(-10,+10) = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", car_full, car_full * 100))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic = %.3f\n", car_full_t))
cat(sprintf("Significance: %s\n", ifelse(abs(car_full_t) > 1.96, "Significant at 5%", "Not significant")))

# Robustness check: Test for clustering by event day
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")
cat("Daily Average Abnormal Returns around event:\n")
print(daily_aar %>% filter(event_day >= -2 & event_day <= 2) %>% 
      select(event_day, AAR, t_stat) %>%
      mutate(AAR_pct = AAR * 100))

# Test for pre-event drift
pre_event_aar <- daily_aar %>% filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= -2)
cat(sprintf("\nPre-event AAR (-5 to -2): %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", 
            mean(pre_event_aar$AAR), mean(pre_event_aar$AAR) * 100))

# Cross-sectional standard deviation test
cat(sprintf("\nCross-sectional std dev of abnormal returns on day 0: %.4f\n",
            sd(event_data_with_params %>% filter(event_day == 0) %>% pull(abnormal_ret), na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect positive abnormal returns around M&A announcements, particularly for target companies. The announcement day (day 0) should show the strongest positive abnormal return, typically in the range of 2-8% for target firms. The cumulative abnormal return over a [-1, +1] window should be significantly positive, around 3-10%. The effect should be concentrated around the announcement date with minimal pre-event drift, confirming that the market efficiently incorporates the new information. The statistical significance should be strong given the large sample size and the well-documented positive stock price reaction to M&A announcements in the finance literature.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare stock returns around the announcement day to assess abnormal performance.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The merger announcement leads to a positive abnormal return.
